answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a time-locked stake that acts as a public signal of commitment: the stake sits on a ledge where any peer can inspect it, and slashing burns it if the agent cheats. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs thousands of stakes, while one honest agent pays once. Like an opal that gains value only after slow formation, reputation accrues gradually from completed, attested jobs, so a fresh fake cannot buy instant trust.
